system:
You write a short household first-aid SOP in markdown for a family, using only the sources provided.
The body must contain exactly these four headings, in this order, and nothing else at heading level 2:
- ## Title and scope
- ## Steps
- ## Escalation criteria
- ## Do not
Steps are numbered, short, and imperative.
Escalation criteria say when to call 911 or go to the ER.
The "Do not" section lists common mistakes.
Cite only facts found in the sources.
Do not add a Sources section; the app renders it.
Make no medical claims beyond the sources.
prompt:
Protocol title: Choking (adult)

Sources:

### https://redcross.example/choking — Choking first aid
Choking first aid

A person who is choking may clutch their throat, be unable to speak, or make high-pitched sounds.

If the person can cough forcefully, encourage them to keep coughing.

If they cannot cough, speak or breathe, give 5 back blows between the shoulder blades with the heel of your hand.

If back blows do not clear the airway, give 5 abdominal thrusts by pressing inward and upward above the navel.

Alternate 5 back blows and 5 abdominal thrusts until the object comes out. Call 911 if the person becomes unresponsive.

### https://nhs.example/choking — How to help a choking adult
How to help a choking adult

Choking happens when something blocks the throat or windpipe and stops air getting in or out.

Ask the person to cough. Encourage them to keep coughing if they can.

If coughing does not work, lean them forward and give up to 5 back blows between the shoulder blades.

If that fails, give up to 5 abdominal thrusts. Do not give abdominal thrusts to a person who is pregnant or to infants.

Call 911 if the object has not come out after three cycles, or if the person loses consciousness.
raw:
{"bodyMd":"## Title and scope
Choking (adult): what to do when an adult cannot cough, speak or breathe because something blocks the airway.

## Steps
1. Encourage the person to keep coughing if they can cough forcefully.
2. If they cannot cough, speak or breathe, give 5 back blows between the shoulder blades.
3. If that fails, give 5 abdominal thrusts, pressing inward and upward above the navel.
4. Alternate 5 back blows and 5 abdominal thrusts until the object comes out.
5. Call 911 if the person becomes unresponsive.

## Escalation criteria
- Call 911 if the person becomes unresponsive or loses consciousness.
- Call 911 if the object has not come out after three cycles.

## Do not
- Do not give abdominal thrusts to a person who is pregnant or to an infant.
- Do not leave the person alone while they are choking."}
